fork_identity.note: branch is transport, not provenance. commit and tree are the identity; source_digests pin the two files that define the scheme so an edited working tree cannot pass as the committed one.

cases.requirement: 1,5. same source, clean builds in different directories
cases.description: two compilations of identical sources, in two randomly named temporary directories, produce the same ids and the same namespace digest -- so no id and no digest carries a build path
two function bodies changed and nothing else; every declaration id is unchanged
every declaration in the library reversed in source order, including class members; no id moves, because no ordinal is an input

cases.requirement: 4. add unrelated declarations -> existing ids unchanged
cases.description: a new top-level function and a new class appear; every pre-existing id survives unchanged and only the new ones are added

cases.requirement: 6. rename -> new identity, exactly as the contract states
cases.description: the contract says a rename mints a new identity with no automatic alias; a rename that silently preserved identity would let a patch bind to a declaration the developer replaced

cases.requirement: 7. same private spelling in two libraries never aliases
cases.description: two libraries each declare a member spelled _secret; each id is qualified by its defining library, so they are two declarations

cases.requirement: 8. generic parameter identity survives a body edit
cases.description: MyClass<T>.method had its body changed; the type parameter id is unchanged, because it is derived from the name and not from a position or a body

cases.requirement: 9. synthesized entities are role-identified or non-addressable
cases.description: every compiler-generated entity either has a defined semantic role derived from its logical declaration, or is explicitly marked non-addressable. None of them claims nominal stability
the id is owner declaration plus source-level name and kind; the lowered procedure name (Ext|get#twice) is recorded as an implementation alias and is never itself an identity

cases.requirement: enum synthesized members vs source-declared elements
cases.description: the elements the developer wrote keep nominal identity, because matrix row DA-15 is about adding one; `values` and the injected `_enumToString` are identified by the enum plus a defined role, not by their generated names
a getter and a setter share a source name and must not share an id; the unnamed and named constructors likewise
the mixin the developer wrote is nominal; any anonymous application class the front end generates is stamped with its role rather than passing as a source-declared class

cases.requirement: private names with an unlinked platform
cases.description: every compilation here runs --no-link-platform, so dart:core is not in the dill. The dart:core-private _enumToString still resolves, because the defining library is read from the reference rather than from an AST node that is absent

cases.requirement: file: libraries are refused rather than path-named
cases.description: the scheme refuses to name a file: library it cannot make root-relative. The alternative -- falling back to the absolute path -- would produce an id reproducible only on the machine that minted it, and it would pass every test written there

cases.requirement: app-root mapping records the mapping, never the path
cases.description: supplying an app root lets a file: library be named app:<relative path>; the root's absolute location is recorded nowhere in the identity block, or the manifest would be machine-specific

falsification.description: the real, unmodified manifest raises no blocking finding -- without this, every arm below would also be satisfied by a detector that flags everything

falsification.requirement: identity derived from a machine/runtime address
falsification.description: an id carrying what looks like an address is refused; a logical identity that moves with the loader is not an identity
an id containing a build path is refused. This is the arm that matters most: such an id passes every test written on the machine that minted it
two declarations sharing one identity means a patch binding to either binds to the wrong one, so a non-zero collision count is blocking rather than advisory

falsification.requirement: lowered extension implementation used as logical identity
falsification.description: naming the lowering would make identity a function of the name-mangling scheme: change the mangling and every extension member silently becomes a different declaration with no source edit

falsification.requirement: synthesized member claiming persistent source identity
falsification.description: a compiler-generated entity relabelled nominal is refused; its name being stable in todays compiler is not a contract

falsification.requirement: manifest bound to a branch instead of a commit
falsification.description: a branch is transport, not provenance -- it moves. The manifest must name a full commit sha

falsification.requirement: a library that could not be named reproducibly
falsification.description: a refusal is blocking: a manifest that silently describes less than the program would let a patch address a namespace nobody checked
an empty manifest cannot testify to anything and must not read as agreement
a patch manifest produced by a different compiler is refused before its ids are compared; agreement across two namespaces means nothing

two distinct private declarations given one id -- what a scheme without library qualification would produce -- is caught as a collision. Recorded honestly: a NATURAL collision could not be constructed in this Dart version, because owner paths already differ, so the qualification is defence in depth rather than the only thing preventing an alias
shapes_tried_without_natural_collision: two classes in two libraries each declaring _secret
two mixins from two libraries applied to one class
a class declaring _x while mixing in another library's _x

falsification.requirement: a surviving declaration whose release/patch ids differ
falsification.description: a single changed id between two compilations of the same declaration is a set difference, which case T02 compares directly and would report
a verdict derived from zero cases would be a statement about nothing, so an empty population is blocking

falsification.requirement: a required test dropped from the run
falsification.description: dropping the private-name case is caught by name; a shorter run must not read as a passing one

verdict.diagnostic_only: cases_run is DIAGNOSTIC. The verdict is a conjunction over every case and every detector; no count or ratio is compared anywhere in this module.
verdict.verdict_rule: stable_identity == ESTABLISHED iff at least one case ran AND every case passed AND every #65 required test and named surface has a case AND no blocking detector finding was raised.

map.verdict: the gate exit code, and whether #65 may be closed
map.cases: verdict.cases_failed, and the per-requirement coverage check
map.findings: verdict.blocking_findings and the gate exit code
map.fork_identity: whether a result may be quoted at all -- a result from a different compiler is a different question
map.manifests: the namespace binding check, and #66's starting namespace
map.falsification: whether the detectors above are known to fire; an never-falsified detector is not known to work
map.schema: readers and later issues consuming this record
map.issue: readers and later issues consuming this record
map.consumers: this check itself, in both directions

consumers.rule: every computed value names the decision that reads it, and every declared consumer refers to a value produced. Checked in both directions.
